 By Nick Wire Nov 19, 2026 • 11:00 am
 Share via facebook Share via X Share via email The Los Angeles Clippers start a four-game road trip tonight in San Antonio against the San Antonio Spurs. 
 The Clippers, now 4-9 overall, won three of their last five games. However, the Clippers have yet to win a road game this year through five games. 
 In their most recent loss on Tuesday against the Utah Jazz, the Clippers gave up 40 points to backup guard Brice Sensabaugh. Sensabaugh  and the Jazz scored 44 points in the fourth quarter, winning by 25 after only leading by two heading into the final frame. 
 The Spurs present a unique challenge for the Clippers as they search for their first road win. Their bench scoring is 18th in the league with about 31 points per game, but their overall scoring ranks seventh in the league.
 Center Victor Wembanyama is averaging 28 points, 12.4 rebounds, and 4.1 blocks per game. Wembanyama's 7'4 stature eliminates easy looks near the rim and forces teams to settle for mid range shots and kick-out threes.
 Clippers point guard Darius Garland is leads the team with 21.2 points and 6.9 assists per game, knocking down nearly 37% from three on about seven attempts per game. 
 Clippers' center Brook Lopez is suited well to counter Wembanyama offensively since he spaces the floor well with his three point shot. Lopez is shooting 41% from three on four attempts per game and his 14.8 points per game ranks second on the team.
 Starting power forward Rui Hachimura also can space the floor for the Clippers. Hachimura is shooting 37% from three on near six shots per game while scoring 13.3 points per game.

 First  pick: Rui Hachimura over 1.5 three pointers made 
 Rundown:  Hachimura averages 2.1 three pointers made per game. With a center of Wembanyamas' caliber guarding the paint, the Clippers will look to space the court which will likely give Hachimura more looks. 
 Second Pick: Keldon Johnson over 5.5 rebounds 
 Rundown: Johnson averages 5.6 rebounds per game for the Spurs. In five of the Spurs' last nine games, Johnson had 6+ rebounds. Lopez and Wembanyama are both very good rebounders who protect the rim well. If Lopez spaces the floor, then the Spurs' forwards will have a better opportunity to grab rebounds in this one.
